messages:
rachel_support: Hey team, customer reported a p95/p99 regression after we rolled out the new client SDK muxing for streaming -> they see huge TTFB variance only for SSE paths. non-stream (sync) looks fine. attaching minimal repro and logs.

mike_eng: Thanks Rachel. Can you paste the raw repro curl/headers? I want to check if the client is sending accept: text/event-stream + multiplexing headers.

rachel_support: Repro (sanitized):\n```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true&client_mux=1'\n```
Observed: first byte ~350ms, then steady stream. If I hit with stream=false or remove client_mux param, TTFB ~45ms. Customer on edge region us-west-2. Logs show repeated 100-101 style keepalives from edge coalescer before first chunk flushed.

jen_sre: do we have any recent change to the edge coalescing window or h2 connection pool settings around that region? Also, is this only SSE or does h2 streaming also show variance?

essential logs:\n```
EDGE_COALESCE: window_ms=30 -> 200ms (overridden by rollout flag)
PROXY_FLUSH: triggered but no payload -> delayed
UPSTREAM_CONN: reused (mux=on)\n```

ash_devex: Interesting — client-side muxing causes small preamble frames and the edge coalescer treats them as noise, bumping the flush timer. Non-stream path bypasses the SSE pathway so flush is immediate. Could be client mux sending 0-length control frames which our proxy collapses.

mike_eng: That matches. We intentionally changed the coalesce heuristic in the rollout to fold small control frames to reduce chattiness; unintended consequence: first payload (first real chunk) is now delayed while coalesce window waits for more payload. Repro steps and quick mitigations:
- temporary: instruct customer to set header `X-Redwood-Stream-Flush: immediate` or use `stream=false` for critical paths
- short-term: rollback coalesce flag in us-west-2 for streaming mux rollout
- mid-term: tweak coalesce logic to ignore control-only frames when deciding flush

rachel_support: Customer asked for a fix this morning. They cannot easily change to non-stream. They prefer a server-side feature flag toggle.

deploy-bot: rollback-flags: scheduled rollback of feature rollout `edge-coalesce-mux-v2` in us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T15:10Z by @jen_sre. CI check passed.

jen_sre: I'll run the rollback and monitor p95/p99 for streaming SSE. Also adding a short synthetic probe that hits streaming SSE with mux=1 and measures first-byte latency every 30s.

mike_eng: Also adding quick guard: if upstream detects only control frames for 2 consecutive windows, force immediate flush on next non-empty payload. I'll open a small PR with a unit test for control frame detection.

ash_devex: For support playbook: if customer sees TTFB > 200ms only on SSE and non-stream is fine, ask for `client_mux` toggle + collect tcpdump and edge logs; tell them we can flip server flag for them while we deploy the fix.

rachel_support: I'll relay options and confirm whether they'd like the rollback or temporary header. Thanks all. Will post customer confirmation here.

mike_eng: Thanks. Follow-ups:\n- jen: rollback + probe (on-call)\n- mike: PR for coalesce control-frame ignore\n- ash: support note + temporary-header docs update\n
rachel_support: Customer chose server-side rollback. Monitor looks good so far: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 58ms in us-west-2 after rollback. I'll close after 24h stability window. :thumbsup:
